lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eEteno planar.\u0: "Planar ethene. All six atoms lie in one plane; the double bond (σ + π) measures ≈ 1.33 Å. The H ends up in the water and the bromide moves away."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eLa base se acerc: "The base approaches the β-H. For maximum overlap, the H and the Br must lie on opposite sides of the C–C bond: anti-periplanar arrangement (H–C–C–Br dihedral = 180°). Try the “Newman” view to see it head-on."
lit.\u0027\u003cstrong\u003eTodo ocurre a la: "Everything happens at once. The lone pair of HO⁻ bonds to the H, the C–H bond breaks, the π bond forms between the carbons and Br⁻ leaves. The σ(C–H) and σ*(C–Br) orbitals are parallel and overlap: the C–C bond order is ≈ 1.5. The other substituents rotate into a common plane (sp³ → sp²)."
lit.\u0027Bases fuertes (HO⁻, RO⁻); bases vo: "Strong bases (HO⁻, RO⁻); bulky bases (tert-butoxide) favor E2 over SN2."
lit.\u0027Bimolecular: la base participa en: "Bimolecular: the base takes part in the rate-determining step."
lit.\u0027Con un sustrato primario como el b: "With a primary substrate such as bromoethane, SN2 competes; 2° and 3° substrates favor E2."
lit.\u0027Geometría anti-periplanar (diedro: "Anti-periplanar geometry (H–C–C–Br dihedral = 180°): maximum σ(C–H) → σ*(C–Br) overlap."
lit.\u0027Un solo paso concertado: la base a: "A single concerted step: the base removes the β-H as the leaving group departs."
lit.\u0027Zaitsev: predomina el alqueno más: "Zaitsev: the more substituted alkene predominates; with a bulky base, the Hofmann product."
